screens.name: Home — unavailable omen and populated omen fixture; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 17 shows the orb-led entry, populated and unavailable omen states, with supplied runtime evidence reporting hero clearance and contrast checks.
findings: Reduce the large-text hero footprint enough to expose more of the omen and its recovery guidance without scrolling.

screens.name: Approach — normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 retains the orb and opening message across captures, while the large variant changes the message from centered to left-aligned.
findings: Keep the opening message alignment consistent across text sizes to strengthen continuity.

screens.name: Ask — self-question input; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 01 and 03 show a labeled question field, recipient control, disclosure and prominent submission action, with the voice alternative below the large capture.
findings: Verify that the voice alternative remains easy to discover after the large-text submission button and with the keyboard open.

screens.name: Ask — named-person question collapsed; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 02 preserves Alex in both the recipient summary and question, but the question uses only an underline rather than the outlined treatment visible in the self-question state.
findings: Make the question's editable affordance consistent between self and named-person states.

screens.name: Named-person editor — normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 02–03 show Someone selected with a checkmark, a labeled Alex field, privacy guidance, confirmation and cancellation.
findings: Keep cancellation discoverable after the confirmation action at 200% text and during name entry.

screens.name: Follow-up card 1 — normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 shows step 1 of 3 and four answer routes, while supplied runtime evidence reports answer acknowledgement and duplicate-request prevention.
findings: Use answer choices on one semantic scale, since Barely started and Nearly certain mix progress with confidence.

screens.name: Follow-up card 2 — normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 05–06 show a clear obstacle question, four separated answers and a persistent 2 of 3 indicator with readable large-text reflow.
findings: Add a captured selected-answer state to complement the reported acknowledgement behavior.

screens.name: Follow-up card 3 — normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 06–07 show the final support question, 3 of 3 progress and explicit wording that an answer leads to the reveal.
findings: Capture the final answer's acknowledgement and handoff to research as one continuous browser sequence.

screens.name: Follow-up other-input — empty, disabled; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 07 shows a labeled free-text field, explanatory disabled-button guidance and Back to choices, with a crowded large-text header.
findings: Place Back to choices on its own row at 200% text to separate navigation from the step count.

screens.name: Listening — voice-start failure; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 18 explicitly reports voice failure and prioritizes typing above retry, while hardware microphone behavior remains unverified.
findings: Supplement this failure state with browser evidence for active listening, transcript review and permission recovery.

screens.name: Planning — loading; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 27 shows a named processing stage, approximate wait, credit reassurance and Cancel, with supplied evidence reporting reduced-motion checks.
findings: Demonstrate the message and recovery offered when processing exceeds the stated one-minute expectation.

screens.name: Research — loading; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 28 distinguishes forecast formation from question planning while retaining the same orb, wait guidance and cancellation pattern.
findings: Show a persistent delay state that explains whether the user should keep waiting or retry.

screens.name: Planning error — normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 10–11 show a clear failure explanation, no-charge reassurance, prominent retry and question editing using intentionally labeled fixture content.
findings: Retain this recovery hierarchy and verify that retry preserves the original question.

screens.name: Prediction error — normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 11 adds Review answers to the retry and edit routes, and supplied runtime evidence reports recovery coverage.
findings: Include an explicit retry capture showing that completed answers remain available.

screens.name: Sensitive-question interruption — planning and prediction; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 31–32 show support as the primary action, alternative question routes and no-credit/no-memory reassurance in both interruption stages.
findings: Place a short explanation before the support button so its purpose is clear before the user reaches it.

screens.name: Forecast reveal — normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 29–30 show the qualified forecast, reminder date, explanation, sharing and revision routes, with sharing receiving the strongest action treatment.
findings: Explain what moderate confidence refers to so it is not mistaken for measured predictive reliability.

screens.name: Evidence index — normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 28–29 separate reasoning, supplied answers, assumptions and sources into labeled rows, while also showing both Back to forecast and Read the forecast.
findings: Clarify the distinction between returning to the forecast and expanding it within the evidence view.

screens.name: Authored reasoning — normal and 200%
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 separates Recorded context, Scenario assumption and Limits, and supplied runtime evidence reports exact text verification from an actual saved local-model response.
findings: Separate the recorded question and answer typographically to make the factual context easier to scan.

screens.name: Authored limits — normal and scrolled 200%
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 shows the complete assumption and explicit absence of external support in the enlarged Limits view.
findings: State what Plus adds beside the upgrade action so Go deeper does not imply stronger evidential support.

screens.name: Legacy reasoning — free Why and Plus evidence reason; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 13–14 and 30 preserve long legacy prose under neutral Passage headings, with supplied runtime evidence confirming complete reading access.
findings: Identify the text as a saved explanation and add a neutral reading overview without assigning unsupported semantic roles to passages.

screens.name: Evidence answers — populated long-content state; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 12 groups full stress-fixture answers beneath their original follow-up questions, and supplied evidence reports complete text and return-focus checks.
findings: Add answer numbering or compact navigation so enlarged long answers are easier to traverse.

screens.name: Evidence assumptions — populated long-content state; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 12–13 show a dedicated assumption page with qualification and a forecast return route, using intentionally long fixture prose.
findings: Use a short introductory label explaining that these are scenario conditions rather than verified facts.

screens.name: Evidence sources — populated long-content state; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 14 explicitly limits source relevance and separates publisher, date, long fixture summary and Open source.
findings: Make each source title the strongest item-level anchor so users can scan a long source list efficiently.

screens.name: Check-in — initial, forecast collapsed; normal, 200% and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 08–09 and 23–24 show the original question above the outcome choices, and supplied browser evidence reports all three choices reachable initially at both sizes.
findings: Add a brief forecast summary beside the question so users can judge the actual prediction without opening another section.

screens.name: Check-in — forecast expanded; normal, 200%, focused and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 08 and 23 expose the unchanged forecast and qualification, with supplied evidence reporting Enter toggling and retained trigger focus.
findings: Offer a nearby jump to the outcome choices after the expanded forecast at 200% text.

screens.name: Check-in — Came true saved; normal and 200%
screens.evidence: Sheets 25–26 show a Saved message and checked Came true row, with supplied evidence reporting replacement, reload persistence and browser pressed semantics.
findings: Preserve the redundant saved text and checkmark when revising this state.

screens.name: Check-in — Did not happen saved; normal and 200%
screens.evidence: Sheets 24–25 show the negative outcome explicitly saved and checked, with supplied runtime evidence reporting persistence and replacement.
findings: Keep the negative outcome visually equal to the positive option to avoid steering users toward confirmation.

screens.name: Check-in — Still waiting saved; normal and 200%
screens.evidence: Sheets 24–26 show the pending outcome saved with explicit wording that the reminder date stays unchanged, corroborated by the supplied browser checks.
findings: Retain the explanation that pending remains open and does not reschedule the reminder.

screens.name: History — empty; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 15–16 pair an explicit device-storage note with a centered empty-state invitation and Ask the Ball action.
findings: Retain the direct first-reading action and the visible local-storage explanation.

screens.name: History — populated single reading; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 15 shows date, original question, forecast and reminder, while the large-text forecast pushes Open check-in beyond the visible area.
findings: Place Open check-in closer to the date or question so the action precedes a long enlarged forecast.

screens.name: History — multiple readings and persisted outcome
screens.evidence: Sheet 16 distinguishes two dated readings and replaces the first reminder with a checked Came true outcome in the persisted state.
findings: Add a 200% capture of the multi-row persisted state to verify its scanning and action placement.

screens.name: Sky — offline samples and selected question; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 36 labels the offline sample boundary and converts the star arrangement into a selected text grid at large size.
findings: Reduce space above the selected question at 200% text so users can see the consequence of selecting a topic sooner.

screens.name: Circles — offline empty state; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 09–10 show offline status, Retry, privacy boundaries and disabled creation and eligibility controls without implying a working social connection.
findings: Explain Friends can ask about me more concretely before users are asked to enable that permission.

screens.name: Age confirmation — normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 18–19 present two explicit age choices and explain that a birthday is unnecessary, but describe protection only as Teen-safe defaults.
findings: Explain Teen-safe defaults in a short, concrete phrase.

screens.name: Onboarding birthday — optional empty form; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 19–20 show optional day, month and year fields, an example, Continue and Skip, with focus visible on the heading.
findings: Keep the optional Skip action discoverable before the three vertically stacked fields at 200% text.

screens.name: Onboarding age blocked — normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 20 explains the age requirement and offers a specifically labeled birthday-correction route.
findings: Retain the explicit correction route and demonstrate its browser focus destination in the next capture.

screens.name: Onboarding birthday correction — normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 21 distinguishes required correction from optional onboarding and shows Check birthday plus a return route at normal size.
findings: Capture invalid-date feedback and keyboard-open access to Check birthday at 200% text.

screens.name: Onboarding focus — unselected; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 21–23 show four focus choices, explicit optionality, progress and Continue without a focus, with the large action extending below the capture.
findings: Shorten the enlarged introductory block to bring the optional continuation action closer to the choices.

screens.name: Onboarding focus — selected; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 22 marks Learning & growth with gold, an underline and a check, while changing the primary action to Meet the Ball.
findings: Keep the primary action fully visible immediately after the selected list when space permits at 200% text.

screens.name: Plans — yearly selected and reading packs; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 26–27 distinguish yearly, monthly and packs with explicit simulation labels, while the enlarged capture starts at the plan section.
findings: Keep the no-real-payments context visible beside the enlarged purchase action and add the monthly-selected state.

screens.name: Share — initial preview; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 33 and 35 show text access, enlargement and download routes, and supplied runtime evidence reports actual PNG export and truthful completion.
findings: Move the privacy summary closer to the preview so it is encountered before downloading at 200% text.

screens.name: Share — scrolled options and invite expansion; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 34 shows download, privacy copy and the expanded Invite & remind section, but the full expanded options are outside the supplied captures.
findings: Capture the complete expanded options, including their focus order and return path at both text sizes.

screens.name: Share — enlarged image inspection and story; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 33 and 36–37 show the full branded image at normal size and a scroll-dependent enlarged page, with a clear return to sharing.
findings: Keep a direct text-equivalent route available from the enlarged image view as well as from the sharing page.

screens.name: Share — image text; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 34–35 expose the forecast, speculative disclaimer and branding as scalable text before Download image, with supplied evidence reporting direct entry and return focus.
findings: Preserve this complete text alternative when changing the exported image design.

screens.name: You — birth profile and populated memory; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 39 separates birth profile, plan and remembered focus, but two large profile actions consume much of the enlarged viewport.
findings: Reduce spacing around the profile actions to make plan and memory sections easier to reach at 200% text.

screens.name: You — empty memory and settings controls; normal and large
screens.evidence: Sheet 32 shows empty-memory guidance, labeled sound/motion/text switches and management actions in a scrolled view.
findings: Give Forget everything a clearly differentiated destructive-action treatment and demonstrate its confirmation state.

screens.name: You — birthday editing; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 38 shows populated date fields with save, cancel and removal routes, while large text places the year and actions below the visible region.
findings: Show validation and save confirmation with the keyboard open at 200% text.

screens.name: You — optional birth details; normal, large and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 37–38 show labeled birth-time and city fields, disabled lookup/save actions and data-sharing guidance, with supplied evidence reporting actual lookup and calculation.
findings: Place explicit requirements beside each disabled action so users know whether time, city text or a selected city is still needed.

components.name: Hero orb
components.evidence: Home and processing sheets consistently use the gold orb as the hero, with supplied evidence reporting motion, contrast and reduced-motion checks.
findings: Make the home orb's actionable role as explicit as its decorative role is on loading screens.

components.name: Tab bar
components.evidence: Main-screen sheets show five persistent labeled destinations and a gold active indicator, while supplied control checks report at least 44×44 browser targets.
findings: Check the crowded large-text labels and raised Ask orb with longer localized destination names.

components.name: Wordmark and balance header
components.evidence: Headers consistently place identity or dismissal opposite balance or test-plan status, with reading balances wrapping to two lines at 200%.
findings: Give the enlarged balance enough width to reduce wrapping and preserve space for the screen task.

components.name: Primary button
components.evidence: Cream filled buttons consistently identify primary actions and disabled variants, with supplied evidence reporting target sizing and several loading/recovery paths.
findings: Provide one consolidated demonstration of focus, press, busy and disabled states for the shared button.

components.name: Secondary action
components.evidence: Secondary actions appear as gold links, centered white text rows and chevron rows across the sheets.
findings: Assign consistent styles to navigation, disclosure and secondary commands so their behavior is easier to anticipate.

components.name: Answer choice
components.evidence: Follow-up choices use full-width separated rows, and supplied evidence reports 180ms acknowledgement, reduced-motion handling and duplicate-request prevention.
findings: Show the selected acknowledgement and keep choices within each question on a consistent semantic scale.

components.name: Question input
components.evidence: Ask sheets show a visible label and readable serif input text, but focused and unfocused fields differ markedly in boundary prominence.
findings: Preserve a clear field boundary when unfocused so existing text still looks editable.

components.name: Large-text input
components.evidence: Large question, name and free-answer fields reflow visibly, with supplied layout evidence reporting exact text doubling and bounded controls.
findings: Demonstrate caret visibility and action access with the browser keyboard open and long input at 200%.

components.name: Settings switch
components.evidence: Sheet 32 pairs switches with descriptive labels and shows Large text selected, while supplied evidence reports immediate reduced-motion behavior.
findings: Capture keyboard focus and state announcements for all three switches, including after reload.

components.name: Omen content
components.evidence: Sheet 17 distinguishes unavailable omen guidance from a populated fixture, but the enlarged home capture exposes little of the content below its label.
findings: Prioritize enough space for the omen's message and next step beneath the large hero.

components.name: Sky star selector and selected question
components.evidence: Sheet 36 shows labeled stars with selected Love and a corresponding question, switching to a text grid in large mode.
findings: Demonstrate keyboard traversal and focus continuity when the star arrangement changes to the large-text grid.

components.name: Circle surface
components.evidence: Sheets 09–10 explicitly label the offline boundary and disable unavailable creation and eligibility controls.
findings: Explain the ask-about-me permission with a concrete example before it becomes available.

components.name: History row
components.evidence: Sheets 15–16 combine original question, forecast, date and reminder or saved outcome within clearly separated rows.
findings: Move the check-in action above long forecast text in enlarged rows.

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Sheets 26–27 show a checked yearly choice, annual total, monthly equivalent, saving and an alternative monthly price in explicit test mode.
findings: Demonstrate monthly selection and its updated continuation label at both text sizes.

components.name: Share preview
components.evidence: Sharing sheets pair a branded thumbnail with enlargement and text routes, while supplied evidence reports a real 1080×1920 PNG.
findings: Expose the text alternative directly from the enlarged preview as well as from the initial share page.

components.name: Notice and recovery
components.evidence: Error, voice and offline states name the limitation and provide visible next steps, with supplied evidence reporting recovery checks.
findings: Extend the same specific guidance to prolonged loading and unresolved permission states.

components.name: Typography and spacing system
components.evidence: The sheets consistently pair serif headings with sans-serif utility text, while large mode creates substantial vertical expansion and several actions below the initial viewport.
findings: Tune large-mode spacing separately from type size to preserve reading order without unnecessarily lengthening every task.

components.name: Atmospheric background
components.evidence: The sheets maintain restrained borderless dark mist and warm gold lighting, with supplied runtime evidence reporting rendered contrast and isolated reduced-motion/performance checks.
findings: Retain the subdued treatment and repeat contrast sampling whenever mist brightness changes.

components.name: Birthday input
components.evidence: Onboarding and profile sheets use labeled day, month and year fields with examples and vertical reflow at 200%, while supplied evidence reports format/error guidance.
findings: Show an invalid-date state and keyboard-open correction without losing the save or check action.

components.name: Age confirmation
components.evidence: Sheets 18–20 provide explicit age choices and a corresponding blocked state with correction guidance.
findings: Replace the unexplained Teen-safe defaults phrase with a concrete description.

components.name: Focus selection
components.evidence: Sheets 21–23 show four readable choices, optional continuation and a selected state communicated by color, line and checkmark.
findings: Preserve the non-color selection cue and verify keyboard selection alongside the reported Back and skip paths.

components.name: Birth-profile surface
components.evidence: Sheet 39 separates Sun sign, age band, birthday and profile actions, with supplied evidence reporting live birth-chart calculation and saving.
findings: Reduce vertical action spacing in large mode so profile management does not dominate the entire first viewport.

components.name: Birth-details form
components.evidence: Sheets 37–38 label local 24-hour time and birth city and explain city-provider disclosure, but only the unfilled disabled state is pictured.
findings: Provide captures of lookup loading, candidate selection, lookup failure and saved confirmation.

components.name: Named-person control
components.evidence: Sheets 02–03 connect the selected Someone option and Alex input to the collapsed About Alex summary and question.
findings: Show empty-name validation and keyboard focus returning to the recipient summary after confirmation.

components.name: Evidence disclosure
components.evidence: Evidence and check-in sheets show labeled disclosure controls and focus rings, with supplied evidence reporting full-text access, Enter toggling and return focus.
findings: Make navigation versus inline expansion consistent in the wording and chevron direction.

components.name: Export status
components.evidence: Supplied runtime evidence reports held, failed, retried and truthfully completed PNG export, but those status presentations are not pictured in the sheets.
findings: Include visible busy, failure, retry and completed export states at both text sizes to substantiate their presentation scores.

components.name: Outcome selection and saved acknowledgement
components.evidence: Sheets 24–26 show all three checked and saved outcomes, while supplied evidence reports aria-pressed, replacement, reload persistence and unchanged pending reminders.
findings: Preserve immediate acknowledgement and reversible selection without introducing an unnecessary save step.

components.name: Reading progress indicator
components.evidence: Sheets 05–07 combine three segments with explicit 1 of 3, 2 of 3 and 3 of 3 text.
findings: Keep progress separate from Back to choices when enlarged and verify that step changes are announced in browser assistive technology.

components.name: Modal-style task shell and back/close controls
components.evidence: Task screens use consistent top-left dismissal plus contextual back routes, with supplied evidence reporting return focus for several disclosure and sharing paths.
findings: Demonstrate dismissal and restored focus for each task family, especially forms containing unsaved input.

components.name: Forecast qualification
components.evidence: Forecast and evidence screens repeatedly display Speculative · moderate confidence, while the share image instead states Not a guarantee.
findings: Define confidence as a scenario judgment or remove the unexplained degree to avoid implying calibrated predictive accuracy.

limitations: All scores are provisional browser assessments based on the supplied screenshots and runtime narrative; no tools, source, prior grades or other task state were inspected.

Each named screen entry includes its corresponding pictured transition and text-size variants; selected, expanded, empty, error, loading and populated states are separated where their task materially differs.

Scores use the frozen six dimensions; A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces, F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility, and overall is 0.4A + 0.6F with null dimensions excluded.
Missing evidence receives a provisional numeric score rather than null; null is reserved for dimensions genuinely inapplicable to a decorative or static component.
Reported browser tests support interaction judgments but were not independently rerun; screenshots alone do not prove persistence, focus behavior, motion, target dimensions or successful actions.
Static transition captures show visual consistency but cannot establish continuous animation quality; the supplied motion and performance results are reported evidence.
Content below a viewport or behind a fixed header in a scrolled capture is not by itself proof of clipping or an inaccessible action; supplied full-layout checks report passing bounds.
Synthetic predictions, repeated stress prose, layout-source labels and fixture notices were treated as test content rather than production-copy defects.
Actual local-model flow and authored sections support structural assessment only; no predictive accuracy, calibrated confidence or production model quality is established.
Active microphone use, keyboard-open forms, several validation states, complete expanded sharing options and visual export statuses are not fully represented in the sheets.
Circles is assessed only as an offline experience; historical social proof and controlled Supabase roundtrips do not establish current production authentication or social behavior.
Physical iPhone, native Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, hardware microphone, haptics, real payments and OS sharing remain unverified; browser scores of 9 do not certify those boundaries.
No repeated novice study is supplied, so no score of 10 is justified.
No hard-gate failure is conclusively demonstrated by this material, but several screens and critical components fall below the authorized browser A>=9 and F>=9 threshold.
topFixes: Explain or remove moderate confidence; its current meaning is unclear and can imply measured predictive reliability.
Tune 200% layouts to reduce decorative and introductory space, bringing omen guidance, history check-in actions and optional onboarding continuation closer to their context.
Standardize secondary navigation, disclosure and editable-field treatments across self, named-person, evidence and sharing flows.
Improve legacy explanation navigation without inventing semantic roles or altering preserved prose.
Complete browser evidence for keyboard-open forms, validation, export statuses, monthly selection and full sharing options.
Preserve the strong authored context/assumption/limits structure and the reversible, explicitly saved check-in outcomes.
